questions.question: How does Words2Wheels use an existing style reward when no semantically similar command is found?

options.A: It uses the closest reward as a template for generating m new rewards, trains their policies in parallel, and assesses whether they beat the temporary retrieved policy
options.B: It rejects all existing rewards and asks a human driver to write a policy
options.C: It immediately executes the nearest policy without further evaluation
options.D: It retrains the LLM on user driving demonstrations before selecting a policy

questions.rationale: The retrieval result provides a temporary trained policy and seed/template for new candidates; RL training and statistical assessment then select the best match.
questions.evidence_quote: The initially selected Style Reward provides a temporary solution since its policy is already trained.

questions.question: What kinds of records does the Driving Style Database store for each driving style?

options.A: A Style Reward code, a pre-trained Style Policy, and analytical statistics such as braking jerk
options.B: Only natural-language commands and raw video recordings
options.C: A policy gradient, sensor calibration, and human preference labels only
options.D: A prompt embedding and a fixed driving trajectory, but no reward functions

questions.rationale: The database contains reward code, trained policy neural networks, and statistical features used for style retrieval and evaluation.
questions.evidence_quote: each record includes a Style Reward, a Style Policy, and analytical data.

questions.question: What is the purpose of reserving test-set natural-driving statistics in the Statistical Evaluation module?

options.A: Provide an objective baseline for judging policy-style metrics while reducing overfitting
options.B: Train every reward function on the same held-out examples
options.C: Replace reinforcement learning with nearest-neighbor imitation
options.D: Ensure the LLM never generates a new reward function

questions.rationale: The reserved set supplies comparison statistics and benchmarks for evaluating alignment without selecting metrics from training performance.
questions.evidence_quote: Using a reserved test dataset, this module prevents overﬁtting and provides benchmarks for evaluating policies.

questions.question: How are user commands and statistical metrics configured in the principal experiment?

options.A: Commands are grouped into three directness levels; GPT-4o uses k=3 retrieved styles and n=2 selected metrics
options.B: Commands are grouped by five risk levels; GPT-4 uses k=2 and n=3
options.C: Commands are grouped into three vehicle classes; GPT-4o uses k=8 and n=15
options.D: Commands are not categorized; the LLM selects every available metric and reward

questions.rationale: The paper defines direct, indirect-strong-hint, and indirect-mild-hint levels; the experiment sets k=3 and n=2.
questions.evidence_quote: We set k = 3 in selecting relevant styles and n = 2 in Statistical Evaluation.

questions.question: What was the role of the reserved test split and repeated RL runs in the policy-alignment experiment?

options.A: 15% of HighD was held out for objective evaluation, and each reward was trained five times with the highest-reward policy retained
options.B: 15% was used for language-model tuning, while each policy was trained once on all data
options.C: The test set contained five events per command, and PPO ran for 15% of each episode
options.D: The authors used a 5% validation split and averaged five independently initialized LLMs

questions.rationale: The experimental setup reserves 15% as test data and repeats RL training with different seeds to address instability, selecting the best reward policy.
questions.evidence_quote: To ensure the objectivity of the Statistical Evaluation module, 15% data was reserved as a test set.

questions.question: In the human preference comparison against IDM, what were the aggregate outcome percentages and event count?

options.A: Words2Wheels preferred in 72%, IDM in 9.2%, tie in 18.8%, across 1,000 events
options.B: Words2Wheels preferred in 64%, IDM in 18.8%, tie in 17%, across 200 events
options.C: Words2Wheels preferred in 79.5%, IDM in 3.5%, tie in 17%, across 1,000 events
options.D: Words2Wheels preferred in 72%, IDM in 18.8%, tie in 9.2%, across 40 events

questions.rationale: Table II reports 1,000 total events and the aggregate preference distribution in that order.
questions.evidence_quote: in 72% events, participants judged the driving style generated by Words2Wheels to be a better match to the user command than IDM.

questions.question: What user-command categories and totals were used in the generalization case-study audit?

options.A: Three directness levels; 10 Level I, 10 Level II, and 20 Level III commands, 40 total
options.B: Three risk levels; 20 Level I, 10 Level II, and 10 Level III commands, 40 total
options.C: Four levels; 10 commands per level, 40 total

questions.rationale: Table III reports 10, 10, and 20 cases for direct, strongly hinted indirect, and mildly hinted indirect commands, respectively.

questions.question: What weakness did the authors observe in some LLM interpretations of driving-style metrics?

options.A: Negative acceleration and jerk values sometimes conflicted with the LLM's interpretation of human intuition
options.B: The LLM consistently treated speed as unrelated to an 'I am late' command
options.C: It could not select a metric unless all reward functions were manually labeled
options.D: It reversed the meanings of braking and lane-change commands in every case

questions.rationale: The case-study discussion notes occasional interpretation errors, particularly when acceleration and jerk are negative.
questions.evidence_quote: when acceleration and jerk values were negative, the LLM’s understanding conﬂicted with human intuition.

questions.question: How successful was the fuzzy-memory test across the three sets of five similar commands?

options.A: All but one case were recalled; the failure was the 'It's snowing and visibility has decreased' input
options.B: Exactly half of the 15 similar inputs were recalled
options.C: All 15 were recalled with no exceptions
options.D: Only one of the three stored memories was retrieved successfully

questions.rationale: The paper reports one exception among the 15 checks, specifically snowing/visibility, while other similar commands succeeded.
questions.evidence_quote:
With the exception
of one case involving “It’s snowing and visibility has de-
creased”, all other test cases were successfully recalled.

questions.question: What scope limitation and next research direction do the authors state?

options.A: Experiments focus on car-following; future work should extend to more complex driving scenarios and refine evaluation/reliability
options.B: The system is limited to highways because urban data were unavailable; future work will remove RL
options.C: Only human-designed rewards were tested; future work will add the first data-driven reward
options.D: The approach has no language component; future work will add command interpretation

questions.rationale: The conclusion describes car-following as the present focus and proposes broader scenarios, finer statistical evaluation, and feedback/reflection.
questions.evidence_quote: Future work will focus on expanding the framework to more complex driving scenarios beyond car-following
